meta.title: Why Camus says a man pushing a rock forever is happy

plates.query: Caspar David Friedrich rocky mountain mist painting

beats.text: A man is condemned to push a boulder up a mountain — forever.
Every time he nears the top, it rolls back down. That is the entire punishment.
Albert Camus said this is a picture of your life.
The commute, the inbox, the chores — the same rock we roll up every single day.
The gods believed endless, pointless labour was the cruellest fate of all.
Camus disagreed. The struggle itself, he said, is enough to fill a human heart.
So picture Sisyphus — at the bottom of the hill, reaching for the rock again — and imagine him happy.

attribution: Albert Camus · The Myth of Sisyphus
